Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attached is our redline (NovaMed_DPA_Redline_v3.docx) and an annotated SCCs file (SCCs_annotated.pdf). Key asks from our side: 

- Confirm processor/processor role language (we've proposed controller/processor split in section 2).
- Confirm whether Redwood can support KMS integration or HSM for customer-managed keys and a high-level implementation window.
- We need a statement of logging/audit capability for access to customer data (retention, redaction policies).
- Please confirm subprocessor list cadence (quarterly vs. on-change) and whether we can receive notices in advance for material changes.
- Are you willing to sign the SCCs as-is, or do you need an Order Form / transfer addendum?

We're trying to keep MSA redlines minimal; this DPA will sit as an exhibit to the Order Form. Procurement would like a timeline for legal's review and a link to the final DocuSign envelope when ready.

Attached files: NovaMed_DPA_Redline_v3.docx (redline) and SCCs_annotated.pdf (comments inline).

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Fwd: NovaMed DPA redline v3 + SCCs annotations — initial legal pass

Rachel / Laura — quick legal pass attached and notes below. I annotated the redline and created SCCs_annotated.pdf with our comments on the standard EU addendum items. High-level: 

- Section 2 (roles): We can accept the controller/processor split but need to add "as set out in Exhibit A" (to avoid ambiguity in order-form context). I'll propose language: "The parties agree the data flows described in Exhibit A govern role allocation; in the event of inconsistency, the MSA controls."
- Section 4.2 (international transfers / SCCs): NovaMed's annotated SCCs introduce additional obligations around encryption at-rest tied to customer-specific KMS. We can commit to supporting customer-managed keys on dedicated/private deployments only. For hosted API customers we need to mark as "where feasible" and propose a security exception path if not supported.
- Logging & audit: We can provide a "logging capabilities statement" (1-2 pages) and evidence (screenshot/export) from our observability console. Ops will need to produce the exports.
- Subprocessor cadence: propose "quarterly notice and immediate notice for any security-critical subprocessors". That balances their ask and our operational model.
- Transfer addendum: Recommend a small transfer addendum rather than reworking the MSA, to keep Order Form footprint light. I'll draft a short transfer-addendum template.

Attachments: SCCs_annotated.pdf (our comments), Legal_DPA_positions.docx (line-by-line alternative wording).

Next steps: if Rachel confirms we can accept "dedicated-only" for KMS commitments for now, I'll prepare the transfer addendum and mark the hosted exceptions. Laura — let me know if tying this to specific order-form IDs (deal NM-2026-834) changes the language.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-22T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovaMed DPA redline v3 + SCCs annotations — Redwood positions and next steps

Sara — thanks for the redline. We did an internal pass and have a few position items below. Ben and Laura are copied. Short version up front: we can accept most of your edits, we propose a short transfer addendum for the SCCs + a small carve for hosted deployments re: customer-managed KMS.

Line items / asks: 

- Roles (Section 2): Accept your controller/processor framework; we will add a reference to Exhibit A (order-form) to avoid future mismatch.
- KMS/HSM: Commitment: "For Dedicated and Private deployments Redwood will support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration) subject to an agreed implementation plan. For Hosted API, Redwood will offer encryption-in-use and standard at-rest protections; customer-managed KMS may be available for enterprise-tier dedicated/private options only." Please confirm if that is acceptable and, if yes, provide the procurement path you prefer for dedicated/private (order-form amendment or separate add-on).
- Logging/audit evidence: We will provide a Logging & Audit Capabilities Statement (one-page) plus two sample exports. Ops estimates delivery by Oct 29, 2026. 
- Subprocessors: We propose quarterly notice + immediate notice for any change that affects access/control. Also: we will provide a current subprocessor list within the DocuSign package.
- SCCs: We prefer to sign the SCCs via a short transfer addendum (attached as a draft). This keeps the MSA/Order Form change minimal.

Requested items from NovaMed: 
- Please confirm whether the transfer addendum (DocuSign link below) is acceptable.
- Procurement contact for final DocuSign wiring (we need contact + purchase order reference).
- Confirm whether NovaMed requires that hosted customers get the same KMS commitment (we currently limit to dedicated/private).

DocuSign (draft envelope): https://example.docusign.com/envelope/123456789
Drive (drafts & evidence): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/novamed-dpa-evidence

If NovaMed can confirm the procurement contact and KMS tolerance by Friday (2026-10-23), Ben and I will finalize the transfer addendum and send the DocuSign envelope the same day.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
